SDF Initialization via Overfitting is a technique for generating a geometric prior for neural fields by pre-training a randomly initialized network to match a target Signed Distance Field (SDF) shape, specifically an inverted sphere, before beginning scene reconstruction [S1].

The claim accurately reflects the information provided in Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that the method initializes model weights randomly and overfits the network for 1000 epochs to an 'inverted sphere' SDF initialization scheme before beginning true training on the scene. It also contrasts this with methods that hardcode the SDF, noting that this specific approach requires a dedicated pre-training phase because the network does not take position as direct MLP input. All specific details in the claim (random initialization, overfitting, target shape, pre-training phase) are present in the evidence.
supported
*   **Strengths:** Enables geometric priors in architectures that cannot hardcode them; improves reconstruction quality compared to un-initialized training [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that RING-NeRF (the method described) does not input position directly into its MLP, unlike NeuS-facto and Neuralangelo which 'hard code' the initialization. Instead, RING-NeRF uses a pre-training phase (overfitting for 1000 epochs) to embed the initialization, thereby enabling geometric priors in architectures that cannot hardcode them. Furthermore, the evidence compares results without initialization to those with it, noting that without initialization, training often results in 'catastrophic failure' or 'way noisier' results with lower PSNR, implying that the initialization improves reconstruction quality compared to un-initialized training.
